Subject: Lumera pilot — Q3 dedicated capacity ask

Kimberly / Marcus / Jonas —

Quick heads-up: Lumera Health (contact: Sara Cho) is moving their pilot from PoC to a 6-week production pilot starting Aug 3. They are requesting a temporary dedicated slice to guarantee latency during the peak window. Key asks from sales/CS: 

- 8 gpus (A100 equivalent) reserved for 6 weeks (2026-08-03 to 2026-09-14)
- Autoscaling exception: no preemption during business hours (8am–8pm PT) so their readiness tests see consistent p99 latency
- Isolation for logs (they asked about separate KV cache controls)

Attached is their capacity spec and our initial runbook. HubSpot: HS-87321.

What I need from you: feasibility on the dedicated carve (Marcus), operational impact and fallback plan (Jonas), and an ask to Product on whether we can grant a temporary autoscale exception without affecting other reserved pools (Kimberly). Marissa — if we approve this, we’ll probably need the Reserved Capacity contract amendment — can you estimate the billing/discount cadence?

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Lumera pilot — Q3 dedicated capacity ask

Thanks Laura — quick read on capacity: at a platform level we can do an 8-GPU carve for 6 weeks but there are three considerations: 

1) Autoscaling exception risk: preventing preemption during business hours will reduce effective utilization and may increase latency for other soft-reserved workloads; we should quantify expected lost utilization (ballpark 18–25% during the window).
2) Model variant fallback: we should supply Lumera a slightly smaller quantized variant we can route to if the carve is exhausted outside business hours. That reduces risk of a hard outage.
3) Scheduling overlap: we currently have two other pilots of similar size in the same region (internal reservations) during August — need final confirmation before blocking.

Proposed next steps: 
- Jonas to confirm whether ops can enforce a weekday business-hours non-preempt policy for that slice.
- Kimberly/Product to approve policy exception (temporary, documented, revert after 6 weeks).
- If approved, I will create the dedicated pool and a model-variant fallback.

I can take the lead on the model variant and quant recommendation.

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

On Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 12:03 PM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Laura — quick read on capacity: at a platform level we can do an 8-GPU carve for 6 weeks but there are three considerations:

Thanks — I can operationalize the carve if Product signs off on the exception. A few operational notes / runbook asks: 

- We need a scheduled maintenance holdback period (2 hours) each Monday at 04:00 PT for hotpatches — Lumera must accept that as part of the carve; otherwise we can't guarantee zero-preempt.
- For the business-hours no-preempt rule: we can enforce via placement policy tied to the dedicated pool tag. Outside 08:00–20:00 PT we can relax the tag and allow eviction. Ops will also require an automated alert to oncall if utilization > 85% for 15 minutes.
- I reviewed the attached runbook; it needs a short section listing who to call on escalation (ops/CS/SE) and an SLO rollback criteria (e.g., if p99 > X ms for 3 consecutive hours).

If Product and Sales agree to those conditions, ops will stand up the pool and add the alerting. If we can't get the maintenance window accepted, we should do a smaller carve (4 GPUs) that we're willing to protect more strictly.

Jonas
Sr. SRE, Production Inference

Folks —

I reviewed Marcus and Jonas' asks with Product leadership. We are prepared to approve a temporary autoscale/preemption exception for Lumera with the following firm constraints: 

- Duration: 2026-08-03T00:00:00-07:00 through 2026-09-14T23:59:59-07:00 (6 weeks).
- Size: 8 GPUs (A100 equivalent) tagged as LUMERA-PILOT-Q3.
- Business-hours no-preempt window: 08:00–20:00 PT weekdays only. Outside this window pool may be used for burst if utilization < 60%.
- Mandatory maintenance holdback: 2 hours Monday 04:00 PT; Lumera must acknowledge this in an amended MSA.
- Ops alerting: automatic paging at >85% sustained for 15 minutes; automatic fallback to model-variant if p99 latency exceeds agreed threshold for >30 minutes.

Conditions: legal and billing amendment must be signed (Marissa), and we will add a one-time operational uplift fee to offset reduced utilization. Once the pilot concludes, the carve will revert and all exceptions removed.

Please draft the amendment and the short runbook edits for Lumera to review. Laura — can you confirm Lumera accepts the maintenance window and the uplift fee?

Kimberly
Head of Sales Ops (acting)
